### 💡 Intuition & Approach
Compute bidirectional CLIP contrastive loss between paired image and text representations using cosine similarity and a learned logit scale.

### ⚡ Python Reference Implementation
```python
import numpy as np

def cs336_l17_symmetric_clip_loss(image_features: list, text_features: list, logit_scale: float = 1.0) -> float:
    I = np.array(image_features, dtype=float) / (np.linalg.norm(image_features, axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
    T = np.array(text_features, dtype=float) / (np.linalg.norm(text_features, axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
    logits = np.dot(I, T.T) * logit_scale
    m_i, m_t = np.max(logits, axis=1, keepdims=True), np.max(logits, axis=0, keepdims=True)
    ce_i = -np.mean(np.diag(logits) - np.squeeze(m_i) - np.log(np.sum(np.exp(logits - m_i), axis=1)))
    ce_t = -np.mean(np.diag(logits) - np.squeeze(m_t) - np.log(np.sum(np.exp(logits - m_t), axis=0)))
    return round(float(0.5 * (ce_i + ce_t)), 6)
```
